package.description:
Follow for more on petrelintide and amylin research.

ZUPREME-1 (Phase 2, 42 weeks; adults with BMI 30+, or 27+ with high blood pressure or high cholesterol, no type 2 diabetes): petrelintide gave up to 10.7% average weight loss vs 1.7% on placebo if everyone stayed on treatment (up to 10.2% vs 1.4% counting everyone). Nausea: 20% vs 6% across doses, mostly mild. Zealand announced the Phase 3 start with Roche on September 22, 2026; as of October 2026 petrelintide is investigational, not approved anywhere.

This content is for educational purposes only and is not medical advice. Always talk to a qualified healthcare professional about your own situation. social.facebook_caption:
Tired of weight-loss headlines that only give you one number?

In the ZUPREME-1 Phase 2 trial, adults with BMI 30+ (or 27+ with high blood pressure or high cholesterol, no type 2 diabetes) taking petrelintide lost up to 10.7% of body weight on average over 42 weeks, versus 1.7% on placebo, if they stayed on treatment. Counting everyone, it was up to 10.2% versus 1.4%.

Petrelintide mimics amylin, a fullness hormone, rather than GLP-1. The real story is tolerability: nausea showed up in 20% of participants across doses, versus 6% on placebo, mostly mild and during dose increases. That's a smaller weight-loss number than tirzepatide's trials show, but these are separate studies with different lengths, not a head-to-head comparison. Tirzepatide's common side effects are nausea, diarrhea and constipation.

On September 22, 2026, Zealand Pharma announced it had started Phase 3 testing with partner Roche. As of October 2026, petrelintide is still investigational and isn't approved anywhere yet.

factcheck.summary: Every number and status line checks out against the primary sources. ZUPREME-1 was a 42-week Phase 2 trial in adults with BMI ≥30, or ≥27 with high blood pressure or high cholesterol (hypertension/dyslipidemia), without diabetes, with all arms on a reduced-calorie diet plus more physical activity (ClinicalTrials.gov). Results: up to 10.7% vs 1.7% placebo on the efficacy estimand and up to 10.2% vs 1.4% counting everyone (treatment-policy estimand), per Zealand's 29 Sep 2026 release on the Lancet publication. Nausea was 79/404 (20%) vs 5/81 (6%), about 80% mild and 73% during dose escalation (Pharmacy Times, News-Medical). The amylin-analogue description matches Roche's 12 Mar 2025 release. Zealand's 22 Sep 2026 release confirms the Phase 3 ZUPREME program was initiated with Roche. Nothing suggests approval anywhere. The tirzepatide comparison is correctly called indirect (separate trials, 42 vs 72 weeks) and names tirzepatide's common side effects. The prescriber line and "Not personal advice" are present. There's no dosing, switching or gray-market content, and the narration is about 150 words. Four minor precision fixes are listed. The CTA is conditional on L1 being live under its exact title, and the pipeline must enforce that.
